caption: Abundant: its proper divisors sum to 16, which is 4 more than 12
Negative $n$: the sign is a unit, as in [[DivisorSigma]]
Large integers: a power of 2 is always 1 short, $2^{41}-1-2^{41}$
The sign classifies: 1 abundant, 0 perfect, -1 deficient
Perfect numbers have abundance 0, as with 496. See [[IsPerfect]]
Zero is outside the domain, so it stays unevaluated
wolfram.note: Both decline: Wolfram's DivisorSigma[1, 0] stays as that call, the mapping's spelling-out of Abundance.
sage.note: Sage's sigma(0) raises: the factorization of 0 is not defined.
sympy.note: SymPy's abundance() takes a positive integer and answers 1 at 0 instead of declining.
